gaps: Architectural/system-level techniques (context management, memory systems, sandboxed execution loops as a distinct category) are thinner than the other Scope categories -- only one directly relevant source (TinyLLM, arXiv 2511.22138) was found, and full technical detail wasn't extractable from the fetched excerpt. Worth a targeted follow-up search if the brief stage needs more depth here.

The RAG survey (arXiv 2510.04905) and Meta-RAG (arXiv 2508.02611) do not explicitly differentiate by model scale/target small models, so their applicability to small-model-specific RAG compensation is inferred rather than directly stated by the authors.

SWE-Compass (arXiv 2511.05459) is cataloged as a unified agentic-coding benchmark, but the granular small-vs-large model performance breakdown could not be extracted from the fetched content -- would benefit from a closer read of its full results tables.

No formal peer-reviewed meta-analysis or systematic review was found directly answering research step 8 (which technique category matters most); the consensus/disagreement picture is assembled from triangulating the NVIDIA position paper, the distillabs fine-tuning benchmark, the Process Verification paper's skepticism of self-critique, and the Devstral/SWE-bench-Pro/SWE-EVO benchmark results rather than from a single source that explicitly compares categories.
summary: Two gathering rounds (initial broad search across all 8 research steps, followed by targeted fetches to extract concrete claims/results and deepen corroboration) produced 22 sources covering all major Scope categories: tool-use/function-calling scaffolding (BFCL leaderboard + underlying PMLR paper, targeted fine-tuning paper reporting 350M model beating ChatGPT-CoT on ToolBench), fine-tuning/distillation (NeurIPS 2025 Spotlight Agent Distillation paper, MapCoder-Lite, distil labs practitioner benchmark), RAG (repository-level RACG survey, Meta-RAG with SWE-bench Lite results), multi-agent orchestration (ProST, MapCoder-Lite's agent-to-single-model distillation), prompting/reasoning scaffolds (SWRV, CoCoS self-correction with two independent venue listings, and a strong process-verification paper with quantified evidence that self-critique harms rather than helps small models), benchmarks (SWE-bench Verified/Pro/Lite/EVO, SWE-Compass, BFCL, ToolBench), named systems (Devstral corroborated across vendor primary source, HF model card, and independent blog with a clear version-over-version SWE-bench trajectory 46.8% to 72.2%; plus Aider/OpenCode/Continue as local-model-capable CLI agents), and the consensus/disagreement question (NVIDIA's SLM-as-default position paper set against harder-benchmark evidence like SWE-bench Pro's sub-20% scores and the Process Verification paper's finding that self-critique is actively harmful for 7-9B models). Most claims have 1-3 independent corroborating sources; a few (Devstral's benchmark trajectory, BFCL methodology, named open-source CLI projects) have 2-3. Remaining gaps are noted above and are minor relative to the plan's success criteria.
